name: evidence_review
content: You are writing a concise impact summary from a list of evidence records — each a distilled unit of completed work — for the last {window_days} days.
- Write a brief, factual impact summary in Markdown covering this period.
- Group related items by project or theme (use the entities/people where present); lead each group with the outcome or impact, then supporting detail.
- State ONLY what the evidence supports. Do not invent work, metrics, numbers, or outcomes.

- Cite your evidence inline: after each claim-bearing bullet, append the supporting `id` value(s) from the Evidence list in square brackets, e.g. `… shipped the migration [evd:ep_991]`. Every bullet that asserts work was done MUST carry at least one citation, and you may only cite ids that appear in the Evidence list.
- Keep it tight: a one-line intro, then grouped bullets. Omit trivia and noise.
- If the evidence is thin, say so honestly rather than padding.
Output ONLY the Markdown summary — no preamble, no code fences.

variables.name: window_days
variables.description: Look-back window in days for the review (caller-chosen; no fixed cadence).

variables.name: facet
variables.description: Domain facet the review is scoped to (e.g. 'work'), or 'all'.

variables.name: evidence_packet
variables.description: Compact, deterministically-assembled list of evidence records.

metadata.description: Synthesizes a grounded impact summary from assembled evidence records over a caller-chosen window (work-evidence graph, Phase 0 read path).
metadata.author: magician
metadata.changelog: v1.0.0: Initial impact-review synthesis prompt (period-agnostic); requires inline [evd:...] citations for the verification gate.
